frames.narration: A developer opens pull request 482. The source host sends an event with a delivery id. The controller handles each delivery id once, so a retried event does nothing new.

The controller creates the namespace pr-482 with a quota of 4 GB of memory and 2 CPUs and a rule that blocks traffic from other namespaces. It asks for credentials that only work for this environment and expire in a day.

A schema for the preview is cloned from the nightly anonymised snapshot. It is a copy-on-write clone, so it takes about 3 seconds and stores nothing until the preview changes data. The migrations of the branch run on top.

The controller deploys the image that CI built for this commit, and only for the services the pull request changed. The other services are the shared stable versions. The preview is serving in about 40 seconds.
The controller registers the host name with the ingress and writes the link and the status on the pull request. No DNS record or certificate is created, because the wildcard covers it.
A reviewer opens the link. The ingress reads the host name and forwards the request to the namespace, which answers from its own schema.
Nobody visits for 30 minutes. The reaper scales the namespace to zero pods. The memory is free for others, and the schema and the route stay.
The next morning the reviewer visits again. The ingress holds the request, the controller scales the namespace back up, and the page loads after about 20 seconds. Later visits are fast.

The pull request is merged. The close event reaches the controller, which deletes the namespace, drops the schema and removes the route and the credentials. If the event had been lost, the reaper would find the orphan on its next sweep.
